question: Could an optical-metric effect accumulate after photons leave a galaxy, making the inferred rotation excess grow with propagation distance?

effective_metric.bending: alpha_gamma is sourced by transverse gradients of Phi_gamma+Psi_gamma and by curl A_gamma
effective_metric.frequency: Delta ln(nu) can be sourced by endpoint A_gamma dot n or by an explicitly time-dependent optical metric
effective_metric.unification_idea: The same optical field supplies a spatial-gradient lensing term and a directional frequency term.
effective_metric.new_physics: Phi_gamma, Psi_gamma, and A_gamma are not ordinary GR potentials unless they are derived from a stable gauge-invariant field action.

sample.per_galaxy_statistic: median fixed-RAR velocity residual over selected outer low-acceleration points

requirements: unsaturated log-path model improves held-out weighted RMS over the distance-independent null
fitted growth over a factor of ten in distance is positive
bootstrap 95 percent upper limit reaches 30 km/s per distance decade
sign is not reversed when Hubble-flow distances are excluded

interpretation_boundary: A null distance trend rejects only unsaturated path accumulation over the sampled 0.98 to 127.8 Mpc range.
An effect that saturates before the nearest SPARC galaxies is not identifiable from this sample.
SPARC radii and baryonic contributions depend on adopted distance, so distance-method subsets and fixed-RAR residuals are required controls.
A successful phenomenological distance trend would still need a covariant field theory and independent redshift, polarization, dispersion, and time-delay tests.
